boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase places and activities on or near UCLA; check each destination’s current access guidance before leaving.

cards.title: Browse the Hammer Museum
cards.subtitle: Westwood, near UCLA
cards.notes: Reserve a little unhurried time for the galleries, then compare one work each and trade observations before heading back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: A free contemporary-art museum visit in Westwood.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hammer Museum states that museum admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission is free; confirm current gallery hours before visiting.

cards.title: See global arts at the Fowler
cards.subtitle: 308 Charles E. Young Dr N, UCLA
cards.notes: Walk the current exhibitions together and choose one object or idea to discuss afterward; the museum lists free admission for all visitors.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission museum stop on north campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fowler Museum’s visitor page says admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday through Sunday; the visitor page lists hours and notes that parking may require payment.

cards.title: Take a garden walk
cards.subtitle: UCLA campus, between Hilgard and Tiverton
cards.notes: Follow the marked paths at a conversational pace, pausing at plant labels or the stream; do not pick or remove any plant material.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-guided nature break on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s events guide identifies the Mildred E. Mathias Botanical Garden as admission-free.
cards.access_notes: The guide says it is open seven days a week and offers docent-led tours on the first Sunday of each month; follow posted garden rules.

cards.title: Inspect space rocks
cards.subtitle: Room 3697, Geology Building
cards.notes: Make a short science detour to see the displayed meteorites, then use the exhibit labels to pick one question to look up together later.
cards.short_summary: A free public meteorite collection in the Geology Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCLA Meteorite Museum says it is open to the public and that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., except federal holidays; its page notes nearby parking is paid.

cards.title: Walk the Murphy Sculpture Garden
cards.subtitle: Northeast UCLA campus
cards.notes: Make a self-guided loop through the outdoor works and let each person choose a sculpture to photograph or sketch from a respectful distance.
cards.short_summary: More than 70 outdoor sculptures across five campus acres.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA’s Go Arts listing labels the Franklin D. Murphy Sculpture Garden as free.
cards.source_title: Franklin D. Murphy Sculpture Garden | Go Arts UCLA
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus sculpture garden; remain on paths and observe any posted site guidance.

cards.title: Try the UCLA SOUNDWALK
cards.subtitle: GPS-triggered public artwork across UCLA
cards.notes: Install the free SOUNDWALK app before starting, then walk a campus route together and notice how the music changes as your location changes.
cards.short_summary: A free app-based artwork that responds to a UCLA walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Go Arts UCLA describes Ellen Reid SOUNDWALK as a free public artwork powered by a GPS-enabled smartphone app.
cards.source_title: Artist Ellen Reid’s SOUNDWALK reimagines what a UCLA walk can be | Go Arts UCLA
cards.access_notes: Bring a GPS-enabled smartphone and headphones if preferred; the artwork covers areas from the residence halls through the botanical garden.

cards.title: Explore the Getty Center
cards.subtitle: 1200 Getty Center Dr, Los Angeles
cards.notes: Book the required timed entry, ride up together, and split time between the galleries, architecture, and Central Garden without buying anything.
cards.short_summary: Free museum admission with a timed-entry reservation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Getty Center states that admission is free and requires a timed-entry reservation.
cards.access_notes: A timed-entry reservation is required. The Getty notes that on-site parking has a fee, so use another transportation option to keep the outing free.

cards.title: Hang at the Beach House playground
cards.subtitle: 415 Pacific Coast Hwy, Santa Monica
cards.notes: Meet at the playground and sandy grounds for a low-key outdoor reset; bring water and use the public beach access rather than paid parking.
cards.short_summary: A free public playground and sandy area by Santa Monica State Beach.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Monica says the Beach House playground and sandy area are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Grounds hours vary seasonally. Parking requires a fee, but the city identifies the playground and sandy areas as free.

cards.entity_name: Annenberg Community Beach House Splash Pad
cards.title: Cool off at the splash pad
cards.subtitle: 415 Pacific Coast Hwy, Santa Monica
cards.notes: Use the splash pad as a quick daytime stop, then dry off in the courtyard or view deck; confirm the gated-area schedule before traveling.
cards.short_summary: A free public splash-pad stop at the Beach House.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Monica says the Annenberg Community Beach House splash pad is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The splash pad is in the gated area, whose hours vary by season and may change on short notice; parking requires a fee.

cards.entity_name: Annenberg Community Beach House View Deck
cards.title: Take in the view deck
cards.subtitle: 415 Pacific Coast Hwy, Santa Monica
cards.notes: Bring a friend for an unstructured ocean-view break, then pair it with a walk along the beach; check gated-area access before you go.
cards.short_summary: A free public ocean-view stop at the Beach House.
cards.evidence_claim: Santa Monica says the Annenberg Community Beach House view deck is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The view deck is in the gated area, which has seasonal hours and possible short-notice changes; parking requires a fee.
